_comment: How a player's ending reads, in BOTH languages: D-PLY-36 and D-PLY-37 (the owner, 2026-10-28).
Read by tests/test_player_endings.py (the helper's observe_first_load over `firstLoad[].batches`,
and the real mpv over `mpv.canary`) and by tests/Model.test.js (Model.outputFailure over
Model.deathReport over every `firstLoad[].reply` and `oldReplies`). A rule written twice gets one
fixture (CLAUDE.md): the helper writes the first-load reply, the model reads it.
D-PLY-37 joins on mpv's PROSE -- the end-file's `file_error` -- so the strings are pinned here
with the mpv version they were read from, and test_player_endings.py runs the real mpv (when it
is installed) to read the audio one again: a later mpv that rewords it turns that test red, not
a channel. `socket[].lines` are mpv's own JSON lines as the shell's socket router reads them,
MEASURED (lane-host5, 2026-10-28, mpv 0.41.0, windowless and silent: a private runtime folder
with no compositor and no sound server in it, --vo=null or a video output that cannot connect,
--ao=null or an output that cannot open) unless the case says `measured: false`. Log text is
mpv's, a trailing newline as mpv sends it. ASCII only: scripts/check.sh refuses anything else in

canary._comment: The audio output that cannot open, in the player's own launch shape: run by test_player_endings.py, which expects `endFile` from the real mpv.

outputErrors.note: In mpv 0.41.0's error table (MPV_ERROR_VO_INIT_FAILED; its error strings are in the binary) and reached by none of the five video output failures measured: a per-file one reads `no audio or video data played` (below) when nothing else can play, and nothing at all when the sound plays on; the player's own --force-window=immediate makes a video output that cannot open an exit before the socket, with no end-file (D-PLY-27).
